question: Should upgrades silently change shared manual-profile execution from three concurrent tabs with a bounded wait to one active tab with an unbounded queue?
rationale: Both choices are technically implementable, but they trade existing-user throughput and fail-fast behavior for stronger serialization and long-Pro-run isolation; repository intent is required.

options.title: Preserve shipped defaults
options.body: Keep three tabs and a bounded queue by default while exposing FIFO serialization and unlimited waiting as explicit configuration.

options.title: Adopt serial unlimited defaults
options.body: Accept one active tab and indefinite queueing as an intentional upgrade behavior, with explicit release notes and live upgrade proof.

options.title: Split policy from fixes
options.body: Land fairness, cleanup, retry, and metadata repairs first, then decide default changes in a separate focused PR.

recommendation.title: Preserve shipped defaults
recommendation.body: Keep three tabs and a bounded queue by default while exposing FIFO serialization and unlimited waiting as explicit configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: He selected and landed the current shared-profile defaults and is best positioned to decide their upgrade contract.
